result.text:
Done. All 58 tests pass (`gradle test`), the 16 original tests unchanged.

## Design

**Repeated commands** — `CommandInterpreter` owns the *syntax* of a sequence (digits, `(`, `)`); `SurveyCrawler` keeps owning only the four basic commands. A digit repeats the last command `digit + 2` more times (`"a0"` → 3 advances, matching the statement's example). The command a digit applies to is an object: `RepeatableLastCommand` repeats it, `NoLastCommand` signals *Invalid command* — so a digit after another digit, after a parenthesis, or at the start is rejected with no null check.

**Sonar / grounds** — `Sonar` (`FirmSandSonar`, `GroundMapSonar`) answers the `Ground` at a position. `FirmSand`, `Silt` and `Boulder` decide what happens when the crawler moves onto them and when it turns on them, so there is no `if` on ground type. Moving asks the ground of the *destination*; turning asks the ground the crawler is *standing on*. How many cells silt slides is a `SiltSlide` (`RandomSiltSlide`, 1..10) — injectable, so the tests are deterministic, with two extra tests over the random one for its limits and its variability.

**Guarded runs** — the crawler holds a `CrawlerRun`: `UnguardedRun` forgets movements and lets it slide; `GuardedRun` remembers the starting facing and every movement, and signals on silt and on a nested `(`. On any failure inside the parentheses the interpreter asks the crawler to undo — the opposite movement of each movement, in reverse, plus the original facing — and passes the exception on. Undoing deliberately does *not* consult the sonar (test 57: a crawler standing on silt before the run must not slide while returning to it).

Cases not fixed by the statement, decided and tested: a digit does not cross a parenthesis (`"a(0)"`, `"(a)0"` are invalid); a stray `")"` is an invalid command; `"()"` does nothing; a finished guarded run is never undone by a later error (`"(aa)x"` keeps its advances); nothing is checked on the cells silt slides over. All are written down in the README, which now documents the second version.

`atFacing(position, facing)` still works and uses a firm-sand-everywhere sonar; `atFacingWithSonar(position, facing, sonar)` is the new factory — that is what kept the original 16 tests untouched.

Two of my new tests failed on the first run because I had mis-traced the expected path (the boulder was not where the crawler actually went); I recomputed both traces and fixed the test data, not the code. I also spot-checked the suite by mutating the silt arithmetic and the undo path — 9 tests caught it.
